lead: Offshore the decisions are yours: which turn, which door to shut, when to leave the yacht, whom to call on which band. Command also brings duties in law.

sections.title: Three turns, and a level lift

qa.q: Which man overboard turn do I use at night if I don't know when he fell?
qa.a: The **Williamson turn**: hard over, at 60° off hard back, and steady on the reciprocal; it brings you back in your own wake. The Anderson turn is for a casualty still in sight.

refs: MOB — recovery by a motor yacht

head: Turn
When
How
rows: Hard over to his side, round 250°, stop
Hard over; at 60° off, hard back; steady on reciprocal
Hard over; at 240° off, hard back; steady on reciprocal

blocks.p: Helm towards the casualty swings the propellers away from him. Williamson and Scharnow bring you back **in your own wake**; the Scharnow in less distance, but only once he is well astern.

fig.title: Scharnow turn from 130°T
lines: Wheel hard to starboard
Reverse it at 130° + 240° = 010°T
Steady on the reciprocal: 310°T
Search back along your own wake

fig.note: High freeboard: stop upwind, beam-on, drift onto him

blocks.p: A high-sided motor yacht drifts faster than a swimmer: stop upwind, beam-on, propellers still, and come down to him. Lift an exhausted casualty **amidships to leeward** in a net on a halyard: the stern slams near the propellers, a vertical lift can collapse him.

sections.title: Shut the space, then count the litres

qa.q: Why must I keep the engine room shut after firing the fixed extinguisher?
qa.a: A **fixed system** works only in a closed space: keep it shut for the hold time while you cool the bulkhead, because opened early the fire reignites.

lines: Stop engines, generator, fans; shut flaps
Count everyone out, then release

blocks.p: A fixed system needs a **closed space**, and the space stays shut for the hold time while you cool the bulkhead: opened early it reignites, and a shutdown at discharge is meant. Under sail put the fire downwind of the crew: fire aft, bow to wind, slow. Use the **fire port**, hatch shut; a lithium battery goes overboard or under plenty of water.

Flooding is litres in against litres out. A patch goes **outside**, where the sea presses it on: a collision mat on lines under the keel; a bulging panel gets pad, board and a shore to a bulkhead. Shut a watertight door once everyone is out. One flooded bow still floats a catamaran: stay aboard. A working keel may drop off: sails down, raft ready, motor gently.

fig.title: How long have you got?
lines: In 650 L/min, pumps 250 L/min: net 400
Lost with 6,000 L more aboard
Distress alert and rafts now

sections.title: Aground, dismasted, no steering, no charge

qa.q: What should I do first when the mast goes over the side?
qa.a: Cut it away, and run no propeller until every line is aboard. Then work out your range under power, reserve kept, and rig a **jury sail** for the rest.

head: Failure
First move
rows: Kedge out, weight aft, off on the tide; engines suck sand
Cut it away; no propeller until every line is aboard
Drogue on a bridle, steered by its legs
Open the bypass valve, ship the tiller; twin screws steer on engines
Nav lights and VHF only; plot on paper

blocks.p: After the top of springs each high water is lower: stranded just after high water, act now or wait a fortnight. Dismasted, work out the range under power, reserve kept, and rig a **jury sail** for the rest.

fig.title: Range under power
lines: Fuel 90 L, keep 20%: 72 L usable
4.5 L/h at 6 kn: 16 h
Port 120 M off: a jury rig as well
No spare belt, 30 h to go
Lights and VHF stay on; plot on paper

sections.title: Leave dry, stay together, hold the course

qa.q: How do I get from a sinking yacht into the liferaft?
qa.a: **Dry**, from the lowest point, one at a time. If there are more people than one raft's rating, launch both and tie them together.

blocks.p: Board the raft **dry**, from the lowest point, one at a time; more people than one raft's rating, launch both, tie them together. First hour: seasickness pills, inflate the floor, a lookout. No water for 24 hours, then half a litre each a day.

fig.title: Cold water: 1-10-1
lines: 1 minute: cold shock, control your breathing
10 minutes of useful movement: swim now
1 hour before hypothermia: then keep still
Alone: HELP, knees up, arms crossed, still
Together: huddle, chests touching

blocks.p: A helicopter pilot keeps station on you: steer what he asks, usually wind 30° on the port bow, and hold course and speed; out of range, close to inside his radius of action. A pale, sweaty, muddled diabetic gets **sugar** while he can swallow.

fig.note: Wind 040°T, 30° on the port bow: steer 070°T

qa.q: How do I send a distress alert beyond VHF range?
qa.a: By **MF DSC** on 2187.5 kHz, then speech on 2182 kHz: that is sea area A2, beyond VHF DSC cover (A1); A3 is covered by satellite.

fig.note: Sea areas follow the coast stations' DSC cover

blocks.p: **Sea areas** follow what the shore hears: A1 VHF DSC, A2 MF DSC beyond it, A3 satellite, A4 the poles. Beyond VHF range distress goes by **MF DSC** on 2187.5 kHz, speech on 2182 kHz. On HF, day and distance want a higher band, night a lower.

list: Sinking, ship in sight: DSC alert and MAYDAY on 16 first, then phone the MRCC.
Alert acknowledged by a coast station: listen, log, help if asked. Unacknowledged, beyond you: relay to the coast station alone.
Medical advice is urgency: DSC urgency call, then PAN-PAN.

fig.title: In the grab bag
lines: EPIRB: registered to you with the flag state
False alert: switch off, tell the MRCC
Radar SART: flashes when a radar sweeps it
AIS-SART: shows with position on AIS screens
NAVTEX: nav, gale, SAR messages always print

fig.title: Silence on channel 16
lines: SEELONCE MAYDAY: casualty or control station
SEELONCE DISTRESS: any other station nearby
PRUDONCE: restricted working may resume
SEELONCE FEENEE: distress traffic ended

sections.title: What the law expects of you at sea

qa.q: Is a yacht skipper obliged to go to help a vessel in distress?
qa.a: Yes: under **SOLAS V/33** you go with all speed, or tell SAR and log why you cannot; you are released once others are tasked.

head: Rule
Duty
rows: Report a navigational danger or unforecast force 10 to ships near and the coast
Go to distress with all speed, or tell SAR and log why; released once others are tasked
Safety decisions are the master's alone
Stand by and help; exchange names and ports; report, records untouched

blocks.p: Your safety orders bind guests too. The **log** is evidence: correct with one line through, the right figure beside, initialled.

fig.title: Correcting the log
lines: 0300 · Course 245°T: one line through it
254°T written beside it, initialled
The old figure stays readable
Never erase or tear out a page

head: Waste
Rule
rows: Never overboard; report every spill and slick
Local rules; MARPOL's 12 M at 4 kn binds larger ships
Plastic never; special area (Med): food waste only, 12 M off, under way

blocks.p: By-laws apply with the COLREGs, to visitors too; a reserve may require its buoys. Dues: LOA rounded up, more for multihulls.

sections.title: The yacht as property and as a contract

qa.q: Which flag do I fly arriving from abroad, and who goes ashore?
qa.a: Fly **Q** from arrival until you are cleared; usually only the skipper lands, with the crew list and passports.

blocks.p: Rules differ by country, principles do not. A yacht flies **one flag**: a new register wants a deletion certificate, a buyer re-registers in time, the original certificate travels aboard. A registered **mortgage** survives a sale: have it discharged before paying. Mortgages rank by date of entry where the register records them.

fig.title: Before the passage: the policy
lines: Limits: area, season; extension in writing
Warranties: skipper's certificate, use, crew
Private pleasure: no paying guests
Hull covers your yacht; third party, others
Disclosure: every material fact, or void

blocks.p: Paid skippering needs commercial papers; under a **bareboat charter** the charterer commands. Paid crew: a signed agreement, 10 hours' rest in 24 in at most two spells, one of 6, repatriation at the employer's cost. From abroad fly **Q**: usually only the skipper lands, with crew list and passports. Schengen: 90 days in 180; VAT-free temporary admission only for boats of non-EU residents.

The award never exceeds the value saved
No danger: towage price; refusal bars a claim

blocks.p: An owner limits liability by tonnage, unless the loss came from his own reckless act.
